b:
A letter
to the daughter
who blossomed in my heart
but never crawled in my lap

Darling daughter,
wherever your little red feet
touch the ground
it should turn to red earth,
not to mud

As you grow,
do not stop
at the limits of classroom learning;
learn the lessons of life
along with it

Speak your mother tongue,
let Tamil grow through you;
learn English for knowledge,
learn many more things beyond it

But do not
let yourself be swallowed by them

Like a bar of gold
in a heap of pearls,
let your Tamil
shine

Learn the scriptures,
learn history too;
anger will rise in you against many,
scatter it by the handful
in your writing

Choose
the field you want.
Even I, tomorrow,
may say "don't";
cut that off as needless talk
and throw it away!
Win, and show us!

The one who leapt into the fire
to ease the worry
of her husband,

and the one who carried in her arms
a man who strayed out of lust
because he was "the husband she married":

the gang of scoundrels
who call them
the very grammar of chastity,
the queens of maidenhood,

spit on them

To show you the way
the footprints
of a thousand good women
stand waiting

Do you want leadership?
Look at Indira.
Do you want to crush those who oppressed you?
Phoolan Devi
stands there smiling

You say that is not enough?

Make a new path
and fight,
let some follow you too

Caste…
sing that it is the scripture of Satan,
say firmly that humankind is one clan;
until equality dawns
make war out loud

In the name of religion
do not forget humanity;
if there is a supreme being,
celebrate that it is one for the whole earth.
You may lose religion,
never lose humanity

This world, my girl, is a camp of predators;
to protect yourself
learn some martial arts.
What you must protect
is not only you
but many sisters like you

The guardians of culture
will climb onto a stage and boil over
that something is wrong with your clothes.
In doubt?
Ask yourself;
your reason will answer

Love anyone,
but
look closely first.
The hasty paddling
of one who jumped in
without checking the depth
is today's
great number of
divorces;
remember that too

The years will pass,
old age will appear;
on that day
teach your own children
these same things

Even if they fix a date
and say you die tomorrow,
do not wither

Say today is mine,
stand up, and work

Even if you plant your flag
on the Himalayas,
give one place in your heart
to this father

That is enough….
note: "The one who leapt into the fire" is Sita, who walked through fire to prove her chastity. "The one who carried … a man who strayed" refers to Nalayini, the legendary wife praised for carrying her unfaithful husband. Phoolan Devi was the Indian bandit-turned-politician who took revenge on her oppressors.
